 You can attach project and GitHub context to a request:
 
 * In the Agents window, select **Folder** or **Repository** to attach another project. An attached project provides request context and doesn't become another workspace root.
-* In any chat input, select **Add Context**, and then select **Issue...** or **Pull Request...**. If multiple GitHub repositories are available, select a repository before you choose the issue or pull request.
+
+* In any chat input, select **Add Context** (`+` icon), and then select **Issue...** or **Pull Request...**. If multiple GitHub repositories are available, select a repository before you choose the issue or pull request.
+
 * Paste a GitHub issue or pull request URL directly into the prompt. The URL remains in the prompt, and VS Code automatically adds the item as a context attachment.
 
 You can attach multiple items. The attachments are preserved in a draft and included when you send the request. Learn more about [starting an agent session in the Agents window](/docs/agents/run/agents-window.md#start-an-agent-session).
```

+++ github_docs::content/copilot/reference/copilot-cli-reference/cli-config-dir-reference.md (new: 47f18d45)
@@ -532,6 +532,10 @@
 
 Host rules and `sandbox.userPolicy.network.proxy` use a built-in local proxy. When both are configured, the local proxy applies the host rules before forwarding traffic to the upstream proxy. Upstream credentials stay outside the sandboxed child process. Host rules and proxy settings are inactive when outbound access is off.
 
+When no proxy is set in sandbox settings, the local proxy selects its upstream proxy from the first non-empty environment variable on the host in this order: `HTTPS_PROXY`, `HTTP_PROXY`, `ALL_PROXY`. Only `http://` and `https://` proxies are supported, not `socks5`.
+
+Destinations matching the host's `NO_PROXY` bypass only this inherited upstream proxy. The sandbox's local proxy still handles these connections and applies its host rules. A proxy configured in sandbox settings ignores `NO_PROXY`.
+
 On macOS and Linux, the sandbox restricts direct connections so programs cannot avoid the proxy. On Windows, the sandbox relies on programs honoring the proxy settings. As a result, programs that ignore the proxy settings on Windows can connect directly and get around your host rules. Windows proxying and host rules also require a supported host and `allowLocalNetwork: true`, which permits private-network access. On Linux, proxy settings reject IPv6 address literals other than the `[::]` dual-stack wildcard. Use an IPv4 endpoint or a hostname with IPv4 support.
 
 Sandbox settings are user-level or enterprise-managed. They are not repository-overridable. For configuration steps and network limitations, see [Configuring Local Sandbox Settings](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/cloud-and-local-sandboxes/configuring-local-sandbox-settings).
```

@@ -13,6 +13,8 @@
 For local testing, set `"experiments.override.chatOpenInAgentsTitleBarLabel": "Try Agents"` in user settings with a fresh profile/data directory. Assignments are refreshed through the assignment service. A triggered scorecard can use `monacoworkbench/experimentTrigger` with `treatmentName == "chatOpenInAgentsTitleBarLabel"`; eligible rendered actions log the trigger in both control and treatment.
 
 The boolean treatment `chatOpenInAgentsTitleBarExpandOnHover` applies to all users, independently of the copy experiment. It defaults to `true`; `false` keeps the action icon-only on pointer hover, while keyboard focus still reveals the label. Tooltips, accessible names, and action behavior remain available. Set `"experiments.override.chatOpenInAgentsTitleBarExpandOnHover": false` to test locally. Its `experimentTrigger` fires on pointer hover in both arms after the assignment resolves.
+
+The experimental setting `chat.titleBar.openInAgentsWindow.richHover` (`experiment: { mode: 'auto' }`) controls what users who are new to the Agents Window (`createdSessionCount < 2`) see when they hover or focus the action. `none` keeps the simple tooltip and the expanding label. The other values show a hover card (`AgentsWindowHoverCard`: a compact graphic, a title, a description, and an Open Agents Window button) and keep the action icon-only, even on keyboard focus. Each is named after its graphic, like the values of `chat.welcomePage.agentsWindowGraphic`: `manyWindowsToOne` shows editor windows for several projects becoming one Agents Window, and `windowComparison` shows the editor window and the Agents Window side by side. The card uses the same managed hover as the tooltip, so it also shows on keyboard focus and can be focused with Cmd/Ctrl+K Cmd/Ctrl+I. Other users always see the simple tooltip, and the action switches as the count or the setting changes. Its `experimentTrigger` (`treatmentName == "config.chat.titleBar.openInAgentsWindow.richHover"`) fires in every arm when a new user hovers or focuses the action. While the card shows, the label never does, so the card arms neither apply nor trigger the copy and expansion treatments. Set `"chat.titleBar.openInAgentsWindow.richHover": "manyWindowsToOne"` or `"windowComparison"` with a fresh profile/data directory to test locally.

role=\"tablist\" data-component-part=\"tabs-list\"\u003e`. When there are\n * more tabs than fit the content width, the list scrolls horizontally but\n * the edge truncates cleanly on the word boundary with no affordance that\n * more tabs exist.\n *\n * Apply a mask-image fade to the trailing edge so clipped content fades\n * out instead of cutting off sharply. region (which contains no tab content), so the\n * visual effect is imperceptible.\n */\n[data-component-part=\"tabs-list\"] {\n  -webkit-mask-image:\n    linear-gradient(\n      to right,\n      #000 role=\"tablist\" data-component-part=\"tabs-list\"\u003e`. When there are\n * more tabs than fit the content width, the list scrolls horizontally but\n * the edge truncates cleanly on the word boundary with no affordance that\n * more tabs exist.\n *\n * Apply a mask-image fade to the trailing edge so clipped content fades\n * out instead of cutting off sharply. region (which contains no tab content), so the\n * visual effect is imperceptible.\n */\n[data-component-part=\"tabs-list\"] {\n  -webkit-mask-image:\n    linear-gradient(\n      to right,\n      #000 If this codebase relies on the `write_todos` tool, the `todos` state channel, or the todo-planning prompt, restore it by importing `TodoListMiddleware` from `langchain.agents.middleware` (not `deepagents`) and passing it to `create_deep_agent`:\\n\\n   ```python  theme={\"theme\":{\"light\":\"catppuccin-latte\",\"dark\":\"catppuccin-mocha\"}}\\n   from langchain.agents.middleware import TodoListMiddleware\\n   from deepagents import create_deep_agent\\n\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(middleware=[TodoListMiddleware()])\\n   ```\\n\\n2. Backend compatibility shims were removed: `BackendFactory`, `BACKEND_TYPES`, `FileFormat`, and `Unset` no longer exist. Replace any backend factories with concrete `BackendProtocol` instances, and add an explicit `namespace` to every `StoreBackend` configuration:\\n\\n   ```python  theme={\"theme\":{\"light\":\"catppuccin-latte\",\"dark\":\"catppuccin-mocha\"}}\\n   from deepagents import create_deep_agent\\n   from deepagents.backends import StoreBackend\\n\\n   # Before (v0.6.x): factory callable, and StoreBackend with no explicit namespace\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(backend=lambda rt: StoreBackend())  # [!code --]\\n\\n   # After (v0.7): concrete backend instance with an explicit namespace\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(backend=StoreBackend(namespace=lambda rt: (rt.server_info.user.identity,)))  # [!code ++]\\n   ```\\n\\n   Also update calls to use the current `ls`, `glob`, `grep`, and `ReadResult` APIs.\\n\\n3. Tool output formats changed: empty `ls` / `glob` output is now the string `No files found` instead of `[]`, and `read_file` no longer renders a fixed-width `cat -n`-style line-number gutter. role=\"tablist\" data-component-part=\"tabs-list\"\u003e`. When there are\n * more tabs than fit the content width, the list scrolls horizontally but\n * the edge truncates cleanly on the word boundary with no affordance that\n * more tabs exist.\n *\n * Apply a mask-image fade to the trailing edge so clipped content fades\n * out instead of cutting off sharply. region (which contains no tab content), so the\n * visual effect is imperceptible.\n */\n[data-component-part=\"tabs-list\"] {\n  -webkit-mask-image:\n    linear-gradient(\n      to right,\n      #000 On a default-agent turn, input tokens drop `,_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`65%`}),` (5,395 → 1,895), validated against our `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://www.langchain.com/blog/how-we-benchmark-deep-agents`,children:`revamped evaluation suite`}),` with no quality regression.`]}),_jsx(Heading,{level:`3`,id:`optimizations`,children:`Optimizations`}),_jsxs(_components.ul,{children:[`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`Lean prompts by default`}),`: The authored base prompt starts empty and tool-usage prose that duplicated tool schemas has been trimmed. Isolated to the default agent’s tool schemas, total description tokens drop `,_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`43%`}),` (4,005 → 2,302); combined with the empty base prompt and opt-in todos, a default-agent turn’s input tokens drop `,_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`65%`}),` (5,395 → 1,895). Tool behavior is unchanged. (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4859`,children:`#4859`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4979`,children:`#4979`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/5009`,children:`#5009`}),`)`]}),`\n`]}),_jsx(Heading,{level:`3`,id:`features-3`,children:`Features`}),_jsxs(_components.ul,{children:[`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/oss/python/deepagents/customization#middleware`,children:`Override a default middleware instance`})}),`: A `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`middleware=`}),` (or subagent `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`middleware`}),`) instance whose `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`.name`}),` matches a built-in now replaces that default in place, rather than erroring on a duplicate. For example, pass your own `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`SummarizationMiddleware(...)`}),` to change the token trigger or summary model without disabling the built-in default. (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4251`,children:`#4251`}),`)`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`Filesystem tools`}),`: New `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/oss/python/deepagents/tools#built-in-harness-tools`,children:_jsx(_components.code,{children:`delete`})}),` tool removes a file or recursively removes a directory (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/3659`,children:`#3659`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/3851`,children:`#3851`}),`); `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`write_file`}),` now overwrites an existing file instead of erroring (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4109`,children:`#4109`}),`); `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`FilesystemMiddleware`}),` accepts a `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`/oss/python/deepagents/overview#virtual-filesystem-access`,children:`tool allowlist`}),` to expose only selected built-in tools (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4325`,children:`#4325`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4698`,children:`#4698`}),`); and reads and searches are tuned for open models — paginated `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`read_file`}),` reports total and remaining lines plus the next `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`offset`}),` (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4540`,children:`#4540`}),`), `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`grep`}),`/`,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`glob`}),` return partial results with a `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`truncated`}),` flag instead of hanging on large trees (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4063`,children:`#4063`}),`), and `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`grep`}),` gains a 1,000-match cap with streamed output and optional context lines (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4570`,children:`#4570`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4706`,children:`#4706`}),`).`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`More prompt-caching support`}),`: Bedrock prompt caching via the `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`deepagents[aws]`}),` extra (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/issues/4108`,children:`#4108`}),`), and automatic Fireworks prompt-cache session affinity (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4598`,children:`#4598`}),`).`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`NVIDIA support`}),`: A built-in Nemotron 3 Ultra harness profile plus NIM app-origin attribution. (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4192`,children:`#4192`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4455`,children:`#4455`}),`)`]}),`\n`]}),_jsx(Heading,{level:`3`,id:`breaking-changes`,children:`Breaking changes`}),_jsxs(_components.ul,{children:[`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`Planning todos are opt-in`}),`: `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`create_deep_agent`}),` no longer includes `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`TodoListMiddleware`}),` by default, so the `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`write_todos`}),` tool, `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`todos`}),` state channel, and todo-planning prompt are absent unless restored with `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`middleware=[TodoListMiddleware()]`}),`. (The OpenAI Codex harness profile still opts in automatically.) (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4929`,children:`#4929`}),`)`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`Backend compatibility shims removed`}),`: Pass concrete `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`BackendProtocol`}),` instances instead of factories, configure `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`StoreBackend`}),` with an explicit `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`namespace`}),`, and use the current `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`ls`}),` / `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`glob`}),` / `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`grep`}),` / `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`ReadResult`}),` APIs. Removed symbols include `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`BackendFactory`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`BACKEND_TYPES`}),`, `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`FileFormat`}),`, and `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`Unset`}),`. New files store string `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`FileData.content`}),`; older `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`list[str]`}),` content stays readable and converts on next write. (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4541`,children:`#4541`}),`)`]}),`\n`,_jsxs(_components.li,{children:[_jsx(_components.strong,{children:`Output format changes`}),`: Empty `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`ls`}),` / `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`glob`}),` output is now `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`No files found`}),` instead of `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`[]`}),`, and `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`read_file`}),` no longer renders a fixed-width `,_jsx(_components.code,{children:`cat -n`}),`-style gutter — update any parsers of raw tool output. (`,_jsx(_components.a,{href:`https://github.com/langchain-ai/deepagents/pull/4561`,children:`#4561`}),`)`]}),`\n`]}),_jsx(_components.p,{children:`Copy the following prompt into your AI coding assistant to migrate a codebase for these breaking changes:`}),_jsx(Prompt,{description:`Migrate a deepagents codebase from v0.6.x to v0.7.`,icon:`arrow-right`,actions:[`copy`],children:'Migrate this codebase from `deepagents` v0.6.x to v0.7 to account for the following breaking changes:\\n\\n1. `create_deep_agent` no longer includes `TodoListMiddleware` by default. If this codebase relies on the `write_todos` tool, the `todos` state channel, or the todo-planning prompt, restore it by importing `TodoListMiddleware` from `langchain.agents.middleware` (not `deepagents`) and passing it to `create_deep_agent`:\\n\\n   ```python  theme={\"theme\":{\"light\":\"catppuccin-latte\",\"dark\":\"catppuccin-mocha\"}}\\n   from langchain.agents.middleware import TodoListMiddleware\\n   from deepagents import create_deep_agent\\n\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(middleware=[TodoListMiddleware()])\\n   ```\\n\\n2. Backend compatibility shims were removed: `BackendFactory`, `BACKEND_TYPES`, `FileFormat`, and `Unset` no longer exist. Replace any backend factories with concrete `BackendProtocol` instances, and add an explicit `namespace` to every `StoreBackend` configuration:\\n\\n   ```python  theme={\"theme\":{\"light\":\"catppuccin-latte\",\"dark\":\"catppuccin-mocha\"}}\\n   from deepagents import create_deep_agent\\n   from deepagents.backends import StoreBackend\\n\\n   # Before (v0.6.x): factory callable, and StoreBackend with no explicit namespace\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(backend=lambda rt: StoreBackend())  # [!code --]\\n\\n   # After (v0.7): concrete backend instance with an explicit namespace\\n   agent = create_deep_agent(backend=StoreBackend(namespace=lambda rt: (rt.server_info.user.identity,)))  # [!code ++]\\n   ```\\n\\n   Also update calls to use the current `ls`, `glob`, `grep`, and `ReadResult` APIs.\\n\\n3. Tool output formats changed: empty `ls` / `glob` output is now the string `No files found` instead of `[]`, and `read_file` no longer renders a fixed-width `cat -n`-style line-number gutter. ### [MODIFICADO] `langgraph::streaming`
- **URL Canónica**: https://docs.langchain.com/oss/python/langgraph/streaming
- **Hash Anterior**: `59b94ff839345f4710848b3463ffe93805ad1b88988dcdaf4e868cda3dc83c16`
- **Hash Nuevo**: `64efe6d26e8f6f3383485e857dc5145d5d7b22e54c42918ced4872485873668e`

```diff
--- langgraph::streaming (prev: 59b94ff8)
+++ langgraph::streaming (new: 64efe6d2)
@@ -1065,7 +1065,7 @@
 In Python versions \< 3.11, [asyncio tasks](https://docs.python.org/3/library/asyncio-task.html#asyncio.create_task) do not support the `context` parameter.
 This limits LangGraph ability to automatically propagate context, and affects LangGraph's streaming mechanisms in two key ways:
 
-1. You **must** explicitly pass [`RunnableConfig`](https://python.langchain.com/docs/concepts/runnables/#runnableconfig) into async LLM calls (e.g., `ainvoke()`), as callbacks are not automatically propagated.
+1. You **must** explicitly pass [`RunnableConfig`](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langchain-core/runnables/config/RunnableConfig) into async LLM calls (e.g., `ainvoke()`), as callbacks are not automatically propagated.
 2. You **cannot** use [`get_stream_writer`](https://reference.langchain.com/python/langgraph/config/get_stream_writer) in async nodes or tools—you must pass a `writer` argument directly.
 
 > **Extended example: async LLM call with manual config**
```
